name: io.shiptrail/shiptrail
title: Shiptrail
description: Live AIS ship tracking and history: any vessel, the ships near any place, port arrivals and trends.

tools.name: search_ships
tools.description: Find ships by name, MMSI (9 digits) or IMO number (7 digits): every ship with a Shiptrail page, any class, on the map now or heard in the last year. Ships on the map now come first. A name may be typed in Latin letters, Japanese kana, Korean hangul, Cyrillic or Greek: ships broadcast their names in Latin letters, so it is searched by its Latin spelling, and readAs says what was searched. Use get_ship with an MMSI for the whole record.

query.description: A ship's name or part of it (3 characters or more; 2 in kana, hangul, Cyrillic or Greek when they spell 3 Latin letters), an MMSI or an IMO number.

tools.name: get_ship
tools.description: Everything Shiptrail's page shows about one ship, by MMSI: identity, size, position, speed, course and status, destination and ETA, where she came from, recent port calls, particulars and registry facts, photo and its credit, a Wikipedia summary, and, with includeNearby, the ships near her. Where she has been is get_track; the ports she called at in the last 180 days, get_port_calls.

mmsi.description: Her MMSI: the whole nine-digit number, not part of it (find it with search_ships).

includeNearby.description: Also list the ships near her. Leave it off unless the question is about her surroundings.

tools.name: search_ports
tools.description: Find ports by name or UN/LOCODE. Busy ports come first, with how many ships are in port, en route and lately departed. Use get_port with a UN/LOCODE for its boards.

query.description: A port's name or part of it, or its UN/LOCODE.

tools.name: get_port
tools.description: A port's Arrivals board (ships in port now, then ships en route by ETA) and Departures board (ships that left in the last 48 hours), as its Shiptrail page shows them, by UN/LOCODE. Each row carries the ship's MMSI for get_ship.

locode.description: The port's UN/LOCODE, such as FIHEL.

limit.description: At most this many rows on each list; the counts are always whole.

tools.name: get_ships_near
tools.description: The ships on the live map within a radius of a port (UN/LOCODE) or a point (lat and lon), nearest first: who each is, where, how fast and which way, and how far off. Positions are from the map's ship list, a few minutes old at most. Read any of them with get_ship.

locode.description: A port's UN/LOCODE, five letters; or give lat and lon instead.

lat.description: Latitude of the point, with lon.

lon.description: Longitude of the point, with lat.

radiusKm.description: How far out to look, in kilometres.

limit.description: At most this many ships, the nearest.

tools.name: get_trends
tools.description: What the live fleet shows now, as Shiptrail's Trends page reads it: the ports where most ships wait at anchor and for how long, the ports most ships are heading for, traffic through the straits and canals, ships stopped in the Southern Bight off Rotterdam and Antwerp, and a group of ships whose broadcast positions show in one false spot. Made about every 30 minutes.

limit.description: At most this many ports, and straits and canals, in each list.

tools.name: get_track
tools.description: Where one ship has been, by MMSI: her positions oldest first, over the last hours (1 to 168) or between two times within the last 180 days (at most 14 days). Each point is a time, latitude, longitude, speed and course, as columns names them. Shiptrail hears ships from receivers near coasts, so open sea shows as gaps; positions are kept where she turned or every few minutes, not every report.

mmsi.description: Her MMSI: the whole nine-digit number, not part of it (find it with search_ships).

hours.description: The last this many hours. Or give from and to instead.

from.description: The window's start, within the last 180 days.

to.description: The window's end; now when left out. At most 14 days after from.

tools.name: get_port_calls
tools.description: The ports one ship called at, by MMSI, newest first: over the last 180 days (or fewer), up to 100 calls, each with when she arrived and left. A call is a stop of 10 minutes or more near a port that Shiptrail heard.

mmsi.description: Her MMSI: the whole nine-digit number, not part of it (find it with search_ships).

limit.description: At most this many calls, the newest.

tools.name: get_area_history
tools.description: The ships that passed within a radius of a port (UN/LOCODE) or a point (lat and lon) over the last 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours, the most recently seen first: who each is, when she was first and last inside, and how close she came. The radius can be up to 25 km near the equator and less towards the poles. Follow any of them with get_track or get_ship.

locode.description: A port's UN/LOCODE, five letters; or give lat and lon instead.

lat.description: Latitude of the point, with lon.

lon.description: Longitude of the point, with lat.

radiusKm.description: How far out to look, in kilometres.

limit.description: At most this many ships, the most recently seen.
